transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um, I hope it's okay that I'm here. I just... I came in because for a long time now, I've been walking around with this sort of flat, heavy feeling. I mean, work is going okay—I'm a management analyst, so I stay busy—and people are really nice to me, so I shouldn't be complaining. But I still just feel down and kind of empty most days. Is that... does that make sense to come in for? I don't want to waste your time if it's just something everyone deals with.
How long have you been feeling this flat, heavy feeling?

Um, well, it's been a while, I guess. Probably about two years and two months? Give or take? It started right around the time I got put on this big dashboard project at work. It ended up putting me in the spotlight a lot more, which was great, you know, a really good opportunity. I was grateful for it. But I guess that's when I started noticing this feeling. I hope it's not silly that I'm bringing up something from that long ago. Is it normal for things to stick around like that?
Do you find yourself enjoying activities or hobbies that you used to like before this flat, heavy feeling started?

Um, yeah, I think so? I mean, I still try to keep up with my hobbies and everything. I still like playing games with my friends online and watching movies, stuff like that. I definitely still get some fun out of it, you know? I really don't want to sound like I'm just sitting around moping all the time, because I'm not. I try my best to stay positive and be fun to be around. 

Is... is it okay that I still enjoy things? Like, does that mean I'm making a bigger deal out of this flat feeling than I should be? I just don't want to be taking up your time if I'm actually doing fine.
Do you feel like you get as much pleasure from those activities as you used to before this flat, heavy feeling started?

Um, yeah, I think it's about the same? I mean, I haven't really noticed a drop in how much fun I have, I don't think. I still laugh at the same stuff and look forward to playing games with my friends. I really try to focus on the good things, you know, so I still get a lot out of it. 

I hope that's... is that a helpful answer? I know people usually say you stop liking things when you feel down, so I hope I'm not confusing things by saying I still enjoy my hobbies. I just really want to be accurate for you, and I definitely don't want to make it sound like everything is terrible, because it's really not.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns since this flat, heavy feeling started?

Um, no, I don't think so. My sleep has been pretty normal, honestly. I mean, I might be a little tired sometimes, but that's just from work, you know? Nothing out of the ordinary. I try really hard to keep a regular schedule so I'm always ready for the next day. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have anything major to report there? Like, I know sleep problems are usually a big thing when people feel down, so I hope I'm not making this confusing by saying my sleep is fine. Am I doing this right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you helpful answers.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite since this flat, heavy feeling started?

Um, no, my appetite is pretty much exactly the same. I'm eating normally, three meals a day, you know? I haven't been overeating or skipping meals or anything like that. I try to make sure I'm eating well so I have enough energy for work and everything. 

Is it... is it weird that my eating habits haven't changed? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to figure this out. I don't want to be wasting your time if all my answers are just "normal." I'm really trying to be as helpful as I can.
Do you often feel guilty or blame yourself for things?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I try to do my best at work and with my friends, so I don't think I have a lot to feel guilty about? If I make a mistake, I just try to fix it and move on. I don't really sit around blaming myself for things, I don't think. 

I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for? I know sometimes people get really down on themselves, but I really try to keep a positive outlook and not let things get to me too much. Is it okay that I'm not experiencing that either? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can do your job.
Do you often feel tired or lacking in energy?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little? I mean, I know everyone gets tired, and I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining about my job or being lazy. I try really hard to stay on top of things. But... yeah, by the afternoon, I do get pretty wiped out. 

It gets to the point where even just doing small things, like fixing a spreadsheet error, or finishing up some expense paperwork... or even getting myself out to soccer... it just feels like I'm dragging my body and my brain through mud. I try my best to just push through it so nobody notices, though. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details, and I hope it doesn't make me sound like a bad employee or anything. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you feel sad most of the day?

Um, yeah... I guess so. I mean, I really try not to let it show, and I don't want to sound ungrateful because I know I have a good job and people are nice to me, but... yeah. That's actually why I came in. 

For a long time now, I've just been walking around with this... this flat, heavy feeling. Like, even when things are going okay, I still just feel down and kind of empty most days. I try to put on a good face so I don't bring anyone else down, you know? But it's just always there. 

Is that... is that the kind of thing you were looking for? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture so you can help me figure this out. Did I explain that okay?
Do you feel like you're interested in things, but just can't seem to enjoy them as much as you used to?

Um, no, not really. I mean... I still enjoy the things I usually do. Like, I play soccer, and I still like going to games and hanging out with the team afterward. I don't think I've lost interest or stopped having fun with it. 

I really try to make sure I'm staying engaged with my hobbies and not just, you know, sitting around all the time. So I think my interest in things is pretty normal? 

I hope that's okay. I know you're trying to get a full picture, and I don't want to mess up your evaluation by not having that symptom. But I still enjoy my stuff, I think. Is it helpful that I'm at least keeping up with my activities?
Do you feel like you're just going through the motions of daily life without any real sense of purpose?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I really try to stay focused on my goals. Like with my work—I'm an analyst—I feel like what I do is helpful to my team, and I really care about doing a good job for them. I definitely don't want to be the kind of person who just coasts or gives up. 

So I feel like I still have a purpose, and I'm actively trying to move forward and be responsible, even if I'm feeling down. I hope that's okay? Like, I know I'm here because I've been feeling so flat, but I promise I still care about my future and I'm trying my best to stay on track. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not confusing things by saying no to that one.
Have you had any thoughts about death or suicide?

Oh, um... no. No, definitely not. I mean, I know I've been feeling really down for a while, but I would never do anything like that. I really don't want you to think I'm, like, a danger to myself or anything. 

I try really hard to keep things in perspective, and I know I have a lot to be thankful for. I just... I just want to feel better, you know? Not... not end things. 

I hope it's a relief to hear that? I know you have to ask, and I'm really glad you're being so thorough. I just want to reassure you that I'm completely safe. Is that... is that the right answer for that one?
Do you feel like your flat, heavy feeling is interfering with your ability to function at work or in your daily life?

Um... well, I really try not to let it affect things. I mean, I want to be reliable, you know? But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, maybe a little bit? 

Like, I had a performance review recently, and they... they did mention that my follow-through hasn't been as good lately. I've been trying so hard to keep up, but I guess some things are slipping through the cracks. And, um, outside of work... I haven't been making it to all my soccer commitments. Or my volunteer stuff. And I was working on MBA planning, but I kind of dropped the ball on that, too. 

I feel really bad about it, honestly. I don't want to be someone who lets people down or just gives up on my responsibilities. I'm really trying to get back on track with all of it. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just being lazy? I really am trying my best to push through it. Is it normal for things to slip a little when you're feeling like this?
How often would you say this flat, heavy feeling occurs during a typical week?

Um... well, it's hard to put an exact number on it, I guess. I really try to have good days, you know? I don't want to sound like I'm just miserable all the time, because I'm really not. 

I'd say... maybe it's there a lot of the time? But I try to just push it to the back of my mind and keep going. Like, I'll wake up and feel kind of weighed down, but I still get up and go to work and try to be pleasant with everyone. So even if the feeling is there most days, I'm really trying not to let it take over. 

I hope that makes sense? I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around wallowing in it every day. I really am trying to stay positive, even when it's tough. Is it okay that I can't give you, like, a specific number of days?
How many days in a row can you typically go without feeling this flat, heavy feeling?

Um... wow, days in a row without it? That's... I guess I haven't really kept track like that. I want to say I have good stretches, you know? I really try to. 

But if I'm being super honest... I don't know if I ever really go a full day without feeling it at least a little bit in the background. Even on a good day, it's sort of just... there. But I promise I don't let it ruin the whole day! I still smile and get things done. I just... I can't really remember the last time I went, like, two or three days completely free of it. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a lost cause or anything? I'm really trying to focus on the positive moments when they happen. Is it bad that I can't think of a clear stretch of good days?
Do you think your flat, heavy feeling is mild, moderate, or severe most of the time?

Um... I definitely wouldn't say severe. I don't want to sound like I'm complaining too much or being dramatic, because I know people have it way worse, and I really do have a lot to be thankful for. 

I guess I'd call it... moderate? It's just that, like I think I mentioned when I first came in, I've been walking around with this flat, heavy feeling for a really long time now. And it's frustrating because even when things are actually fine—like, work is going okay, or people are being super nice to me—I still just feel down and kind of empty most days. 

I really try to shake it off and appreciate the good things, I promise I do. It just sort of lingers. Does moderate sound like the right word for that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answer.
Do you feel like you have to force yourself to enjoy activities that you used to find pleasurable?

Um... I wouldn't say I have to *force* myself, exactly. I mean, I still do things! I still hang out with friends sometimes, and I try to keep up with my hobbies. I don't want to sound like I've just given up on having fun or anything. 

I guess... maybe it just takes a little more effort than it used to? Like, sometimes I'll agree to go do something, and in the back of my mind I'm kind of just going through the motions, even if it's something I usually like. But I always try to smile and make sure everyone else is having a good time, you know? I don't want to bring anyone else down. 

So, I don't know if "force" is the right word... maybe just that the enjoyment doesn't come as naturally as it should? I hope that's an okay way to explain it. I really am trying to stay engaged with things, I promise.
How long do these periods of feeling down and empty usually last when they happen?

Um... wow, how long do they last? I guess... well, it's hard to say exactly. I don't really time it or anything, because I really try not to dwell on it, you know? I want to focus on the positive stuff. 

But if I had to guess... I don't know, it just kind of feels like it's always sort of... there? Like it doesn't really have a clear beginning and end, it just sort of hums along in the background for... a really long time. Weeks, maybe? Or months? I'm honestly not sure if I have a good answer for that. 

I hope that's not frustrating for you? I just... I don't want to make it sound like I'm constantly miserable for months on end, because I'm really not! I still have good moments. It's just that the empty feeling doesn't really fully go away. Is it okay that I don't have an exact timeframe?
Do you feel like you have to make an effort to find pleasure in things that you used to enjoy?

Um... I feel like we might have just talked about this a little bit, but... yeah, I guess I do have to make an effort. 

I don't want it to sound like I'm totally numb or anything, because I really do try to find the good in things. I still go out and I try my best to be present. It's just... maybe it doesn't happen automatically anymore? Like, I have to consciously remind myself, "Hey, you like this, you should be having fun." 

I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much. I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need. Does that make sense, the way I'm explaining it?
Can you describe a recent day when you felt the least flat and heavy, and how that compared to your usual days?

Um... a recent day where I felt the least flat... gosh. I really want to give you a good example here, but... my mind is kind of drawing a blank. I'm so sorry, I hope that's not unhelpful. 

I'm sure I've had decent days recently! I really do try to stay positive and make the best of things, so I don't want to sound like I'm just complaining. But... they kind of just all blend together, I guess? It's just that the baseline is always sort of... that same heavy feeling in the background, even when I'm trying to have a good time. 

I really don't want to sound pessimistic, I promise I'm trying to think of one. Maybe I'm just not paying close enough attention when the better moments happen? Is it alright if nothing specific comes to mind right now? I can definitely keep thinking on it if you need me to come up with something.
